newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO holds steady despite crude losses.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO holds steady despite crude losses.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Tuesday were expected to hold steady in spite of crude losses as swaps suddenly firmed in late afternoon trading, traders said.
"Paper is quite resilient," said a trader after October contracts were traded at $113.50 and $114, rebounding to Monday's closing levels. Levels at midday were lower at $112- $113.
"I do not know whether the paper is reflective of the physical," said a western trader.
"The fuel oil market seems to have a mind of its own ... it does not seem to be moving in tandem with crude," said a Singapore trader.
Fundamentally, traders said there were sufficient supplies, particularly with more physical oil arriving In Singapore from Bahrain, Kuwait and Fujairah at the end of September.
On Monday, cst 180 fuel oil supplies for loading in October were bid/asked at $113/$114 per tonne.
"There should was a lot of oil around," said a trader.
But demand from China was resurfacing on Tuesday, traders said.
"With crude coming off, Chinese buyers are expecting lower prices and are seeking end September/early October cargoes," a trader said.
The run up of crude prices recently have kept Chinese buyers out of the market and stocks have since been depleted, he said.
Some trade was rumoured at $124 per tonne on cost-and-freight basis to South China but this was doubted by the market as current bids were around at $120-$122.
Traders said there was not much activity heard in the Singapore market although there were a few spot requirements on a c-and-f basis.

Taiwan sold 38,000 tonnes of 3.0 percent sulphur fuel oil lifting October 1-10 at "close to $116 per tonne", an official said, much higher than its last sale at $93.50-$94 for August lifting. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-8703086)
